1mbbj5y:230: Sparse attention has long faced a "train-inference objective mismatch" problem: although routing scores in the chunk selection stage participate in top-k retrieval, they do not directly participate in the final attention weight computation. As a result, the backpropagation signal from the LM loss cannot effectively guide the routing module to learn "which chunks to choose". HiLS uses hierarchical softmax decomposition to expose the chunk quality proxy in the inter-chunk allocation term directly in the forward computation graph, allowing routing parameters to receive gradient signals from the main loss. This design is not a simple engineering optimization; it fills a long-standing theoretical-loop gap in sparse attention at the training methodology level.

A common problem with these methods is that they compress all token information within a chunk into a fixed vector, losing inter-token interaction patterns and spike signals. The learnable compressed chunk key in HiLS, through a first-order LogSumExp approximation, essentially learns a selector for "which token information is worth keeping". With entropy-based calibration, the model can automatically judge the distribution shape inside a chunk—smooth aggregation for uniform distributions, extreme-value preservation for spike distributions.
